purpose: Source-grounded route lookup for Fix My Stream; documentation facts, not customer telemetry.
limitations: Not an operational test of any account or destination.
Unknown/null means not established by reviewed documentation, not unsupported.
Documentation listings are not proof an integration is currently available to every account.
The inventory covers documented streaming routes, not all unrelated product features or every customer-specific enterprise configuration.
Refresh current provider requirements before prescribing settings or purchasing a plan.

methods.name: Browser Studio
methods.path: Browser camera/mic/screens/media/guests → Studio composition → selected destinations.
requirements: 720p30 at 4 Mbps; 720p60 at 5 Mbps; 1080p30 at 6 Mbps, set automatically by Studio.
1080p requires Professional+. Stream quality is locked while live.
Restream recommends at least 10 Mbps upload, 25+ for Full HD; a speed test does not prove sustained transport health.
Mobile guidance: Chrome on Android, Safari on iOS.
first_checks: Check browser-visible devices, permissions, scene/source toggles, chosen output quality and where the first defect appears.
notes: OBS encoder controls do not apply to browser Studio. Studio 4K local recordings do not mean 4K live output.

methods.name: External encoder
methods.path: Software/hardware encoder → selected Restream stream card → selected destinations.
requirements: Use that stream card’s URL/key or documented authorized integration. A new card has a new key; reusing a card retains its key unless reset.
Common RTMP guidance: H.264, CBR, 2-second keyframes, AAC. Destination requirements override a generic preset.
first_checks: Match the actual encoder to the intended Restream card/event, then inspect ingest and each destination.
Compare OBS network, rendering and encoding counters separately.
notes: One source feed is replicated in the cloud. Dual feeds, backup encoders, remote production and uploads can add local bandwidth or load.
The generic 15,000 Kbps table is not a universal hard cap.

methods.name: Pre-recorded video
methods.path: Upload/import a file or reuse a recording → schedule video → cloud playout → destinations.
requirements: MP4/MOV/M4V/MKV, H.264 video, AAC audio, 2-second keyframes. Validate source encoding; a container extension alone is insufficient.
Upload & Stream tiers govern capacity. Documented Premier/Marathon/Media libraries: 2/4/12 hours; maximum resolution 1080p/1080p/4K.
Looping: Marathon/Media, up to 10 repeats; looping article states a 40-hour cap. Destination duration limits still apply.
first_checks: Check upload processing, source media properties, actual file selection, timezone/start time and destination activation.
A manual-start destination still requires its own Go Live action.
notes: Playout runs in the cloud while the laptop is offline. Low laptop upload during playout is not automatically the cause.
Restream recommends 15–20 seconds of intro/outro padding for ingestion delay.
Scheduled social posts: Facebook Profile/Page, YouTube, LinkedIn; other platforms differ.

methods.name: Live Webinar
methods.path: Live Webinar setup → Studio → dedicated attendee link and optional Slack.
requirements: Separate webinar add-on. Documentation snapshot: 100 attendees $99/month; 500 $299/month; 1,000 via custom Enterprise. Verify account billing.
No Pairs support for this workflow.
first_checks: Identify the correct webinar/attendee link, capacity and Slack channel if used.
For a speaker request, inspect backstage admission and host controls.
notes: The completed event keeps its replay link; a later webinar gets a new invitation link.

methods.name: RTMP ingest
requirements: Server URL and stream key are separate fields unless the encoder requires a combined URL.
first_checks: Check exact stream card and redacted error; never ask the user to paste the key or private URL.

methods.name: RTMPS ingest
methods.path: Encoder → encrypted RTMP transport into Restream.
requirements: Available on all Restream plans; use the RTMPS URL supplied by the selected card.
first_checks: Check TLS-capable encoder and exact URL scheme.
notes: Input encryption does not by itself prove every output leg is encrypted.

methods.name: SRT ingest
methods.path: SRT-capable encoder initiates delivery to Restream using the supplied connection details.
requirements: Business or custom Enterprise. H.264/AAC; H.265 input is documented with conversion to H.264 for incompatible outputs.
OBS Custom: full supplied SRT URL in Server, stream-key field empty.
Incoming AES-128/256 supported with the Restream-generated passphrase. Suggested SRT latency 700 ms, maximum 1,300 ms.
first_checks: Confirm input direction, plan and exact endpoint fields in the encoder locally.
Do not invent a Restream SRT Pull/Listener setup; use the provider-supplied push configuration.
notes: The article’s Caller-only wording must not be interpreted as a general statement that no server listens for incoming packets.
Protocol SRT differs from .srt subtitle files.

methods.name: WHIP ingest
methods.path: WHIP encoder → Restream → native-compatible or converted RTMP outputs.
requirements: All plans; beta. OBS WHIP service: supplied Stream URL; Bearer token left empty for this documented input.
Video H.264/VP8/VP9; audio Opus/ALAW/ULAW. This list applies to WHIP input, not RTMP input.
first_checks: Check WHIP support in the encoder and actual input/output route.
notes: Restream documents automatic RTMP conversion where required. Sub-second/one-second marketing latency is not an end-to-end promise.

methods.name: Pre-recorded playlist
methods.path: Up to 40 ordered video entries → scheduled cloud playlist → destinations.
requirements: Marathon or Media Upload & Stream add-on; up to 24 hours per playlist.
Files/order editable only before live; graphics/chat can be edited during playout.
first_checks: Check entry order, total duration, encoding and processing of the failing segment.
notes: No blending with a live presenter. No native playlist loop; duplicate entries within the 40-entry limit. Back-to-back playlists have a documented 2-minute gap.

methods.name: Studio landscape + portrait
methods.path: One Studio session → 16:9 and 9:16 destination groups.
requirements: Professional+. Assign orientation before live; active-channel orientation cannot be changed during the stream.
Graphics/elements are shared across orientations.
first_checks: Inspect both previews and each channel’s assigned orientation.
notes: Paired channels receive the primary landscape feed. Different graphics per orientation are not supported.

methods.name: OBS landscape + portrait
methods.path: OBS plus Restream Vertical plugin → landscape and portrait ingest → assigned channels.
requirements: Guide provides macOS/Windows builds and requires current OBS. Select Restream.io service.
Primary OBS audio mixer is shared; separate vertical audio inputs not supported. Encoding parameters inherited, but vertical bitrate can differ.
first_checks: Inspect both monitor tabs and actual vertical source; a Portrait assignment alone falls back to the primary landscape feed if no vertical plugin output arrives.
notes: YouTube Landscape + Portrait produces separate events and combines their chats. Allow for additional encoding/network workload.

methods.name: Encoder feed inside Studio
methods.path: Encoder or Zoom → Studio RTMP Source → Studio composition → destinations.
requirements: Business/custom Enterprise; one RTMP Source at a time.
Source guidance: 720p up to 60 fps (2,800 Kbps at 30, 4,500 at 60 recommended); 1080p up to 30 fps, 4,500 Kbps recommended; AAC; 2-second keyframes.
first_checks: Use the Studio source credentials, not an unrelated encoder stream card.
Confirm the source appears and is included in the active scene before debugging destinations.

methods.name: Zoom meeting/webinar into Restream
methods.path: Zoom custom live-streaming service → Restream encoder card OR Studio RTMP Source.
requirements: Zoom account admin enables custom live streaming. Eligible paid account and host Meetings/Webinars license required by the guide.
Zoom asks for a playback-page URL; it does not determine the complete Restream destination list.
first_checks: Confirm direction and host/license permissions.
Check whether copied credentials belong to a standalone encoder card or Studio source.
notes: Zoom → Restream is different from the Zoom Events/Webinars Plus incoming-destination feature.

methods.name: Mobile streaming
methods.path: Mobile browser Studio OR a mobile encoder → Restream.
requirements: Browser guidance: Android Chrome / iOS Safari. Encoder apps have separate licenses and controls.
Larix combines URL/key with a slash; mobile Streamlabs uses separate fields in the guide; Wirecast Go custom RTMP requires payment.
first_checks: Identify app versus browser, foreground state, camera/mic permissions and thermal/network conditions.
Inspect URL-field format locally without exposing credentials.

methods.name: Console gameplay
methods.path: Console → capture card or Remote Play on desktop → OBS/Studio → Restream.
requirements: Capture card: console HDMI out → card in; card USB → computer; add capture source.
PS Remote Play: Windows/macOS; not every game/peripheral supported. Xbox guide uses Windows Xbox app.
first_checks: Compare capture/Remote Play preview with program output before testing Restream.
A black capture feed can be source/HDCP configuration; follow console/device documentation for gameplay capture.
notes: This guide does not establish a direct arbitrary-RTMP broadcast from the console.

methods.name: Audio-first Studio show
methods.path: Mic/mixer or recorded audio → Studio with avatar/image/video background → destinations.
requirements: One audio input per participant; an extra camera can add another source.
first_checks: Check intended mic and live audio; hiding a camera/participant avatar does not mute audio.
notes: An audio-first show can still transmit a video canvas; do not remove the video track without destination support.

methods.name: Record without broadcasting
methods.path: Studio → recording in storage; no destination broadcast.
requirements: Paid plans; guide also documents a limited Free trial. Standard up to 6 hours; Professional/Business up to 10.
first_checks: Confirm Record only versus Go Live.
A successful recording checks production, not destination ingest or playback.

methods.name: Local Studio recordings
methods.path: Individual participant devices → upload recording segments → host downloads.
requirements: Professional+; beta; desktop Chromium recommended, mobile participants excluded during beta.
Studio only; local CPU/storage used; participant must finish uploading segments.
first_checks: Check device/browser and incomplete uploads before declaring lost recordings.
RTMP sources, graphics/layouts and cloud-storage media are not included as local source tracks.
notes: 4K recording capability is separate from Studio live output resolution.

audio_guidance: AAC; Restream recommends 96 Kbps, at most 160 Kbps.
first_checks: Identify standard RTMP, WHIP beta, or direct Enhanced Broadcasting path.
Compare channel playback with Restream preview; check Disconnect Protection only if already configured.
notes: Restream guide states a 48-hour maximum. Higher-resolution/beta claims in that guide require route-specific verification.

platforms.name: Vaughn Live
platforms.connection_route: Named manual server/channel URL and key.
eligibility_and_plan: All Restream plans.
video_guidance: 720p recommended or 1080p; CBR 1,500–2,500 Kbps; 30/60 fps; keyframes 2 seconds; High profile.
first_checks: Use the selected server’s URL and correct channel key.
Set title/category on Vaughn.

platforms.name: Vimeo
platforms.connection_route: Paid Restream Custom RTMP/RTMPS; create an encoder event on Vimeo.
eligibility_and_plan: Paid Restream plan and a Vimeo account entitled to live streaming; exact Vimeo plan not specified in the Restream guide.
video_guidance: Restream recommendation: 1080p30, 5,000 Kbps, keyframes 2 seconds.
first_checks: Verify Vimeo live entitlement, event preview and the event’s own URL/key.
notes: No Restream analytics or title updates through the custom route.

platforms.name: X
platforms.connection_route: Account authorization.
eligibility_and_plan: Verified X Premium account required by Restream’s guide.
video_guidance: 720p30 recommended; up to 1080p, but 60 fps only at 720p; H.264/AVC.
Keyframes 3 seconds; 9,000 Kbps recommended, 12,000 maximum in the Restream guide.
first_checks: Check Premium/verification and broadcast comments rather than replies to the announcement post.
Do not assume the common 2-second recommendation is X’s stated recommendation.
notes: Title up to 256 characters; descriptions not displayed. No advance event post from Restream.

platforms.name: YouTube
platforms.connection_route: Authorize the channel owner; manager/editor access is insufficient for this documented integration.
eligibility_and_plan: Enable live streaming and complete verification; first activation may take 24 hours.
video_guidance: CBR; keyframes 2 seconds recommended, at most 4; up to 60 fps. AV1/HEVC ranges are separate and do not prove codec support across Restream.
audio_guidance: YouTube guidance: AAC or MP3; stereo 128 Kbps at 44.1 kHz; 5.1 uses 384 Kbps at 48 kHz. Verify full route codec/layout support.
first_checks: Check channel owner, live enablement, event identity and selected latency before bitrate changes.
For dual output, inspect the correct landscape or portrait YouTube event.
notes: Restream states only streams shorter than 12 hours are archived automatically; archive limit is not the live duration.
Restream OBS dual output creates two YouTube events with combined chat. Shorts/vertical is a format, not another service.

platforms.name: Zhanqi.tv
platforms.connection_route: Named in Restream’s central catalog; current channel-specific setup not verified.
eligibility_and_plan: Eligibility, regional access, account approval and provider plan are not established by the catalog listing.
first_checks: Confirm that this destination is actually available in the user’s Add Channel screen.
Obtain current provider encoder setup and exact error text before proposing connection or encoding settings.
notes: No dedicated setup article found in the 14-collection inventory. The integration link redirected to the generic Choose how to go live article. Listing is not proof of a currently operating integration.

platforms.name: Zoom
platforms.connection_route: Restream → paid Custom RTMP → Zoom Incoming livestream; distinct from Zoom → Restream.
eligibility_and_plan: Zoom Events or Zoom Webinars Plus, Unlimited or Pay Per Attendee. Host/co-host setup access.
Zoom desktop Windows/macOS/Linux 6.2.0+ per Restream guide; verify current minimum.
video_guidance: Guide gives upload-speed recommendations of 4 Mbps for 720p30 and 6 Mbps for 1080p30; these are not video bitrate limits.
first_checks: Enable Incoming livestream in the Zoom session and copy its URL/key.
Join the event; use More → Incoming livestream → Send live after the feed arrives.
notes: An ordinary Zoom meeting subscription does not establish access to this incoming route. Restream guide contains a stray Vimeo authentication sentence; verify Zoom-specific requirements.

custom_protocols.name: Custom RTMP/RTMPS
requirements: Paid Restream plan; provider-issued URL and key; authentication only when required by that provider.
first_checks: Check endpoint scheme, exact event/key and provider-side preview/start.
notes: No API-dependent chat/analytics/title management. The destination must actually support ingest.

custom_protocols.name: Custom SRT
requirements: Business/custom Enterprise; provider-issued srt:// destination URL.
first_checks: Confirm outgoing direction and provider endpoint.

The custom-channel form documents separate Stream ID/passphrase fields, while the SRT FAQ says per-output latency/encryption configuration is unavailable. Verify the actual contract with Restream before promising those controls.
notes: Do not transfer incoming SRT’s AES/latency capabilities to every output.

custom_protocols.name: Custom HLS
requirements: Business/custom Enterprise; provider must support HLS ingest at the supplied http(s) URL.
first_checks: Confirm this is an ingest endpoint, not a viewer’s .m3u8 playback URL.
notes: This output route does not establish HLS/m3u8 source ingestion into Restream.

custom_protocols.name: Custom WHIP
requirements: All plans; provider-issued http(s) WHIP endpoint; beta.
first_checks: Check endpoint capability and authentication requirements with provider; do not copy the empty-token input rule to arbitrary outputs.
notes: Restream explicitly does not recommend this beta for production-grade workflows. No guaranteed end-to-end latency.

delivery_and_operations.name: Website Embed Player
facts: Business/custom Enterprise; Business includes 1,000 concurrent viewers aggregated across embedded sites.
One active Embed Player channel per stream. Persistent channel iframe; no chat, viewer analytics supported.
Documented guidance: at most 12,000 Kbps, 30 fps, keyframe interval no less than 2 seconds; latency up to 60 seconds.
Guide states 14-day maximum player stream duration; this does not guarantee the upstream encoder connection lasts that long.
first_checks: Check enabled player channel and actual iframe.
Offline state before input and click-to-unmute are expected; a viewer-counter here excludes social-platform viewers.

delivery_and_operations.name: RTMP Pull for production
facts: Professional: 3 links; Business: 5; Enterprise: custom. Up to 10 active connections per link.
Pulls the account’s active feed for production or monitoring. Public website embedding is explicitly disallowed by the guide.
first_checks: Check that the source account is live and use the pull link as a media input, not an ingest destination.
For a public website, use Embed Player rather than publishing a private pull link.

delivery_and_operations.name: Guest channel pairing
facts: Host requires paid plan. Each free guest can add up to 3 channels; paid guest limits follow their plan. Up to 20 guests / 100 paired channels.
Supported for Studio and encoder streams, including scheduled; not pre-recorded or webinars.
Supported incoming chats can appear as Paired; host replies only to own channels; no relay between host and guest channels.
Turning off the invitation toggle disables the link, not previously paired channels. Studio dual output sends paired channels primary landscape.
first_checks: Inspect host and guest activation separately. A host-disabled channel can still appear on to the guest.

delivery_and_operations.name: Per-destination transcoding
facts: Separate hourly add-on, not included in a base plan; unavailable for Organizations per current guide.
Documented configurable maxima: 1920×1080, 60 fps, video 6,000 Kbps, audio 320 Kbps.
Hours are consumed per destination; guide says exhaustion disconnects the stream. Added delay is reported around 2–3 seconds, not a guarantee.
first_checks: For incompatible destinations, verify which fields can actually be changed and enough remaining hours.
Do not equate rotate with a separately composed portrait layout or promise sample-rate conversion from bitrate controls alone.

delivery_and_operations.name: Disconnect protection
facts: Business/custom Enterprise; RTMP/SRT encoder streams. Configure before live.
Fallback windows: 5, 15 or 30 minutes. Business uses default video; custom video via Enterprise.
Fallback loops until recovery/window expiry; when expired, destinations end. Trigger is automatic source loss.
first_checks: Inspect whether protection was enabled and whether its time window has elapsed.
Do not promise manual triggering, failover alerts or exported failover metrics.

delivery_and_operations.name: Backup encoder
facts: Custom Enterprise; two distinct encoders, preferably independent networks; RTMP or SRT.
RTMP uses the supplied primary/backup keys; SRT uses two supplied URLs. Not available for browser Studio.
Monitor shows primary/backup source identity. Guide does not guarantee continuous operation beyond 24 hours; custom long-duration needs must be confirmed.
first_checks: Inspect active-source indicator and independent backup feed.
A long destination duration cap is not an uptime guarantee.

delivery_and_operations.name: Destination proxy
facts: Custom Enterprise; channel-level route setting applies across stream drafts.
first_checks: Use only for a supported destination-route issue after locating the first failing hop; it is not a fix for local render lag.

delivery_and_operations.name: Simultaneous-channel and plan limits
facts: Public channel caps: Free 2, Standard 3, Professional 5, Business 8; Enterprise negotiated.
Connected channels and simultaneously active channels are different counts. Facebook Pages and Custom RTMP need paid access.
Professional adds Studio 1080p and dual format. Business adds embed and Studio RTMP source. Add-ons and provider subscriptions are separate.
first_checks: Check the actual account’s plan, activated channels and add-on balances.
Do not infer a plan from a missing button alone or treat a marketing price as an account quote.

limits: No local OBS/device inspection, stream-key retrieval or RTMP/SRT credential entry.
Published MCP tools do not expose detailed ingest health. UI/public API status and bitrate/FPS are separate capabilities; discover actual authorized schemas.
Viewer/message analytics are not transport diagnostics.

chat_matrix.caveat: Replies via Restream may require viewers to refresh LinkedIn; an older FAQ still says read-only.

documented_audio_conflict.scope: Comparison of published guidance, not proof every nonconforming stream is rejected. Sample-rate guidance also differs (44.1 vs 48 kHz).

documentation_conflicts.title: Legacy Teams Live Events wizard
documentation_conflicts.decision: For a new event, use current Teams RTMP-In policy and provider setup. The old creation wizard is retired; pre-June-30-2026 scheduled events have a documented exception through February 28, 2027.

documentation_conflicts.title: YouTube bitrate columns have different codecs
documentation_conflicts.decision: The Restream general table labels H.264 near ranges matching YouTube AV1/H.265. Use the owner’s codec-specific table; do not describe every range as H.264.

documentation_conflicts.title: Generic encoder FAQ omits WHIP
documentation_conflicts.decision: The dedicated WHIP guide establishes beta WHIP input; do not repeat the generic only-RTMP-and-SRT statement.

documentation_conflicts.title: Generic 15 Mbps and pass-through claims
documentation_conflicts.decision: Generic encoder examples are not global hard caps. Explicit transcoding, protocol conversion and Instagram adaptation are exceptions to broad pass-through language.

documentation_conflicts.title: SRT output passphrase versus no per-output controls
documentation_conflicts.decision: The custom-SRT form mentions Stream ID/passphrase, while the SRT FAQ denies per-output latency/encryption settings. Preserve the disagreement; verify supported output behavior before promising encryption controls.

documentation_conflicts.title: LinkedIn reply support versus older read-only FAQ
documentation_conflicts.decision: Current capability tables say read/reply, with a viewer-refresh caveat. A read-only state can still require checking the actual connection; the old FAQ is not sufficient proof of universal lack of replies.

documentation_conflicts.title: CBR incorrectly labelled sample rate
documentation_conflicts.decision: CBR is a rate-control mode, not a Hz sample rate. Keep sample-rate requirements unknown until verified with the provider.

documentation_conflicts.title: Standard Twitch versus Enhanced Broadcasting
documentation_conflicts.decision: Do not treat a standard RTMP recommendation as the cap for direct Enhanced Broadcasting, or assume enhanced codecs and resolutions are supported through Restream.

documentation_conflicts.title: Upload, live, recording and continuity limits differ
documentation_conflicts.decision: A 24-hour playlist cap, 40-hour loop cap, 14-day player cap, recording length and encoder maintenance window describe different parts of the route. Use the applicable smallest limit without inventing a universal uptime guarantee.

documentation_conflicts.title: Latency promises are route-dependent
documentation_conflicts.decision: General under-two-second claims do not override documented transcoding delay or up-to-60-second player latency. Measure the actual path; audio/video offset is a separate issue.

documentation_conflicts.title: Generic slower-preset advice can worsen load
documentation_conflicts.decision: The quality article groups a slower encoder preset with lowering load. For x264, slower generally costs more processing; use the OBS performance playbook and measure the actual encoder instead of copying that phrase.

documentation_conflicts.title: Ten channel links lack specific setup evidence
documentation_conflicts.decision: Every checked catalog-only integration URL redirected to the generic streaming-method guide. Record current activation, eligibility and numerical encoder limits as unverified; do not fabricate them.
